dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: monitor.py domain #7 'EM-Gravity Coupling κ' hardcodes kappa_obs = 10.9 / 6.5 (the only place the 2017 BOU value appears in code). Domain #10 'Eclipse Magnetic Anomaly (Aug 12 2026)' computes ecm_eclipse = -18.22 * 0.95 * 1.672 = -28.9 nT with formula label 'ΔB = -18.22 × coverage × FSF'. Note -18.22 = -10.9 x 1.672 (the dome's 2026-03-28 κ correction already applied), and the trailing 1.672 sits in the FSF slot where EBR's FSF is 1.029 - i.e. the ×1.672 correction is applied twice and FSF is dropped. This is the mechanical origin of the -28.9 nT value KS-005 lists as one of 'three different values'. observed is the hardcoded string 'PENDING' and pass is hardcoded None; there is no code path that fetches INTERMAGNET data or ever updates this domain, so the dome's post-eclipse 'observed=PENDING, days_remaining=-45' status (monitor/changes/latest-poll-summary.txt) is structural, not a pending analysis. Domain #12 fetches real-time NOAA Kp (latest 1-minute value), not the eclipse-window Kp, so it cannot evaluate the Kp<2 precondition for a past date.

holes_found.description: Both Kp statements in our WIN-010 text are contradicted by the GFZ Potsdam definitive Kp record, and they're wrong in the direction that inverts our asymmetric-evidentiary-standard argument. (a) data/wins.json id=010 detail_evidence: 'the 2017 eclipse observation underlying WIN-010 was recorded at Kp ≈ 3', repeated in detail_verdict_text para 4 ('The 2017 baseline underlying this WIN was recorded at Kp ≈ 3'). GFZ definitive Kp for 2017-08-21 (kp.gfz.de/app/json, fetched 2026-09-26): 00Z 2.333, 03Z 2.333, 06Z 3.0, 09Z 2.667, 12Z 1.667, 15Z 1.333, 18Z 2.0, 21Z 2.667. The BOU eclipse ran 16:24-19:14 UTC with maximum at 17:47 UTC (Skyfield/DE421 computation this run), and the dome's -10.9 nT minimum is at 17:20 UTC, inside the 15-18Z slot where Kp = 1.333 (1+). Kp 3.0 is the daily maximum, ~10 h BEFORE the eclipse. 'Recorded at Kp ≈ 3' is false for the observation itself. (b) detail_evidence final paragraph calls 2016-03-09 'a genuinely Kp<2 quiet day', and detail_verdict_text's closing note repeats 'Kp<2 quiet day'. GFZ 2016-03-09: 00Z 2.0, 03Z 1.667, 06Z 1.333, 09Z 1.333, 12Z 2.0, 15Z 1.667, 18Z 1.333, 21Z 1.667 (previous day peaked at 2.333). The GUA eclipse ran 00:22-03:00 UTC (max 01:52), inside the 00-03Z slot at Kp = 2.0, which isn't < 2. By the eclipse-window reading, the 2017 event met Kp<2 and the 2016 event did not, the opposite of what our text says. The dome itself classifies by local BOU standard deviation (2016 std 2.23 nT vs 2017 8.05 nT, live wins.html WIN-010), not by Kp, and our text adopted the dome's quiet/storm framing and attached Kp numbers to it that don't match the record. Why critical: WIN-025 in our own review audits the dome's Kp premise against GFZ and finds it 'factually incorrect' (data/wins.json id=025 field detail_verdict_text, 'Dome Author Update' paragraph). A defender can apply the same 30-second GFZ lookup to WIN-010 and show we made the same class of error twice, which is a hypocrisy attack on the review's rigor, not just on this WIN.
holes_found.recommendation: Replace both Kp statements with the GFZ eclipse-window values and cite the GFZ Kp service. Suggested text: '2017-08-21: Kp 1+ during the 15-18 UT slot containing the BOU eclipse maximum (17:47 UT) and the reported minimum (17:20 UT); the day's peak of Kp 3 occurred at 06-09 UT. 2016-03-09: Kp 2o during the 00-03 UT slot containing the GUA eclipse (max 01:52 UT).' Then rewrite the asymmetric-standard paragraph. The honest version is stronger for us: the dome's quiet/storm split tracks local BOU variance, not Kp, and under the dome's own Kp<2 wording the 2016 re-anchor doesn't qualify while the 2017 anchor it discarded arguably does (eclipse-window reading). Mirror WIN-025's GFZ-audit framing so the two WINs apply one method. Snapshot the three GFZ JSON responses (2016-03-08..09, 2017-08-21, 2026-08-09..12) into data/dome-api-snapshots/ or an equivalent reproducibility location before citing them.

Meanwhile the poller is recommending a silent_ignore / tacit_withdrawal verdict against the dome for the same eclipse cluster (monitor/changes/latest-poll-summary.txt, IMMINENT WINDOW WATCH block). A defender will point out that we're being silent too. Separately, the dome's precondition failed: GFZ Kp for 2026-08-09..12 peaks at 3.0 (08-11 15Z), 08-12 peaks at 2.667 (03Z), and the eclipse slot (18-21Z, European maxima 17:58-18:54 UT) is 2.333. The dome's 'Kp < 2 entire Aug 9-12 window' (Tier 3) and 'valid only if Kp < 2 on August 12' both fail, and its 'IF Kp ≥ 3 ... not a falsification' clause leaves 2 ≤ Kp < 3 undefined, so the eclipse-slot value falls in a gap in the dome's own rule. Our detail_evidence warned that the Kp filter is 'an escape clause that voids the test whenever geomagnetic activity is elevated', and it has now fired. The WIN text doesn't say so.
holes_found.recommendation: Add a dated post-event status paragraph now, even before the full analysis: (i) eclipse occurred 2026-08-12; (ii) GFZ Kp values above, with the dome's precondition failed under both of its stated readings, plus the Kp 2-3 gap in its rule; (iii) the dome has posted no result, and its monitor.py cannot post one (observed hardcoded 'PENDING', no fetch path); (iv) the status of OUR pre-registered nine-station test, including either the result or an honest 'evaluation overdue, expected by <date>'. Convert the future-tense pre-registration sentences to past tense ('we pre-registered...'). Route the actual INTERMAGNET evaluation to analyst as a commissioned item, because it's now the load-bearing deliverable for this WIN, KS-005 and the eclipse-2026 page. Keep the Kp caveat symmetric: our frozen B1-M-001 amplitude_caveats[3] also treats Kp ≥ 2 as noise-inflating rather than falsifying, so we can't hold the dome's escape clause against it while using the same one ourselves.

holes_found.description: Our text makes an unsourced claim that the 2017 BOU signal tracked the eclipse, and the dome's own audit says the opposite. data/wins.json id=010 detail_evidence: 'Data from INTERMAGNET confirms this mechanism: the −10.9 nT signal tracks the eclipse shadow geometry with the correct amplitude, timing, and spatial pattern.' No analysis or citation backs this. The live dome page disowns the 2017 signal: PROS-003 (monitor/baseline/02-wins.txt line 73) says 'Timing audit shows Z minima uncorrelated with eclipse geometry across 2017 and 2024 events (scatter −180 to +111 min from totality). Anomalies attributed to geomagnetic storm contamination, not eclipse signal', and live WIN-010 (line 222) says 2017 was 'storm-contaminated, zero tracking stations'. On timing, the dome's -10.9 nT minimum at 17:20 UTC is 27 min before the BOU eclipse maximum at 17:47 UTC (Skyfield/DE421, 93.6% obscuration), so detail_claim's 'coincident with eclipse maximum' (the dome's original claim, raw-text/02-wins.txt line 81) is wrong by roughly half an hour. Our endorsement of 'correct ... timing' therefore contradicts both the ephemeris and the dome's later audit. The 2026-07-19 update paragraph says the dome 're-anchored' but leaves out WHY: the dome withdrew the 2017 event as storm contamination. That omission matters because the reason is a dome self-contradiction (see stronger_arguments[0]).
holes_found.recommendation: Delete or source the 'tracks ... with the correct amplitude, timing, and spatial pattern' sentence. If no one has run the 2017 multi-station timing analysis, replace it with the Sq-framework prediction ('the Sq framework predicts a depression of this order near eclipse maximum at ~94% obscuration under midday sun') and don't claim empirical confirmation. Add to the dated update: 'The dome withdrew the 2017 event on 2026-03-15, stating that its own timing audit found Z minima scattered −180 to +111 min from totality and attributing the anomaly to storm contamination (PROS-003).' Note the 17:20 vs 17:47 UT offset. Given the GFZ record in hole 0 (Kp 1+ at eclipse time), the dome's 'storm contamination' attribution is itself questionable, which parallels WIN-025.

holes_found.description: The pre-registered discrimination test has two uncontrolled confounds that both run in FSF's favour. Our text defines residuals as '(observed delta_Z) / (baseline × coverage), under the simplest linear-coverage approximation applied identically to both models' and commits that 'If FSF beats the magnetic-latitude prediction ... something non-trivial will need explaining' (data/wins.json id=010 detail_verdict_text para 7). (a) Coverage inputs: the dome's per-station 'coverage' values (raw-text/03-predictions.txt lines 23-31; also used as dome_coverage in predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json B2-M-001) understate true obscuration badly at northern stations. Skyfield/DE421 max-obscuration (area fraction) vs dome coverage: EBR 100% vs 95, SPT 98.8 vs 90, COI 97.1 vs 92, HAD 94.4 vs 80, CLF 92.9 vs 70, NGK 85.4 vs 40, ESK 91.0 vs 55, LER 88.3 vs 42, Canary/GUI 69.3 vs 72. The ratio true/dome is 2.13 at NGK, 2.10 at LER and 1.65 at ESK, and correlates with FSF at Pearson r = 0.84. A residual built on the dome's coverage values would inflate exactly where FSF predicts larger values and could manufacture an FSF 'win'. The text never says whose coverage values the residual uses. (b) Solar elevation: the sun stood 3-14° above the horizon at eclipse maximum at every European station (NGK 3.4°, EBR 4.8°, SPT 7.2°, CLF 7.3°, COI 10.5°, HAD 12.7°, ESK 13.6°, LER 14.2°), compared with 57° at BOU 2017 and ~70° at GUA 2016. Sq E-region conductivity scales roughly with cos^0.5 of the solar zenith angle, so a near-sunset eclipse should produce a much smaller signal than the midday BOU baseline. Neither the dome's linear formula nor our ensemble-median comparator (Kim & Chang's ensemble, dominated by daytime events) accounts for this. Sun altitude also correlates positively with FSF (r = 0.39). Both confounds mean an 'FSF tracks better' outcome can arise without any dome physics, but the text has committed to reading that outcome as dome-favourable.
holes_found.recommendation: Since data now exists, any fix is post-hoc and must be labelled as such. Recommended disclosure: (1) report the residual test exactly as pre-registered, stating which coverage values were used; (2) report a second, labelled-post-hoc version that uses NASA Besselian-element obscuration (eclipse.gsfc.nasa.gov local circumstances) and a solar-zenith-angle factor, and explain why; (3) state in the WIN that the dome's own coverage inputs are wrong by up to ×2.1 at NGK and LER. That error is independent of mechanism, so the dome's per-station predictions fail on geometry inputs alone, which strengthens our case. Remove or qualify 'something non-trivial will need explaining'. Have analyst cross-check these obscuration numbers against NASA or Jubier before publishing (Skyfield/DE421, WGS84 sea level, no limb profile; method sanity-checked: Paris 92.1%, London 91.4%, BOU-2017 93.6%, Madrid/Bilbao at the totality edge).

holes_found.description: CROSS-SURFACE (not WIN-010 text, but it feeds this WIN's pre-registration): our own frozen, OTS-anchored claim B1-G-005 appears to fall outside its own tolerance. predictions/eclipse-2026-08-12-predictions.json bucket_1_standard_physics.geometric_predictions[4] registers Hartland (51.00N, 4.48W) maximum obscuration ≈ 88% ± 2 percentage points (review_cross_ref data/sections.json part4 §4.2.7 'peaks at ≈ 88 % obscuration'), and docs/eclipse-2026/index.html repeats 'Hartland 88%, claim B1-G-005'. Skyfield/DE421 gives 94.4% area obscuration at 18:15 UT (magnitude 0.949), which is 4.4 pp above the registered centre and outside the ±2 pp band. The same method gives Paris 92.1% and London 91.4%. If an independent check confirms this, a claim we OTS-anchored and presented as 'a scored, timestamped forecast' missed its own bound. That's precisely the kind of item a defender will pick out of a frozen file to argue 'your pre-registration failed too'.
holes_found.recommendation: Before anyone publishes eclipse results, have analyst verify Hartland obscuration against NASA's Javascript Solar Eclipse Explorer or Xavier Jubier's local-circumstances calculator. If ~94% is confirmed, disclose it prominently on docs/eclipse-2026/index.html and §4.2.7 as a scored miss on B1-G-005. The file is frozen and must not be edited; this is the canary-by-example working as intended, and owning the miss is worth more than the claim was. Also check where the 88% came from (possibly a magnitude/obscuration mix-up or a different location).

holes_found.description: The magnetic latitudes our text labels 'CGM' are centered-dipole values, and true CGM changes the band membership. detail_verdict_text: 'we will evaluate each of the nine stations at its CGM magnetic latitude (IAGA observatory registry)' and then 'Centered-dipole computation with IGRF-14 epoch 2020 pole (80.65°N, 287.32°E) gives station CGM latitudes: COI 43.7°, EBR 42.9° ...'. These are two different coordinate systems. AACGM-v2 (aacgmv2 Python package, epoch 2026-08-12, 0 km; checked against Tromsø 67.1° and Boulder 48.1°) gives EBR 33.3, SPT 31.1, COI 32.0, CLF 42.8, HAD 46.7, NGK 47.9, ESK 51.9, LER 57.5, versus the text's 42.9/42.4/43.7/49.6/53.6/51.85/57.5/61.8. In western Europe CGM runs 4-10° below dipole latitude. On a 30-50° band, HAD and NGK move from out/marginal to clearly inside, ESK is just outside, and the Canary station drops far below 30° (AACGM is unreliable that close to the equator; dipole gives 33.2). That gives a 6-in / 2-out-high / 1-out-low split rather than the text's 5-in / 3-out / NGK-marginal split, and HAD, which the text names as a key endpoint station, is no longer an out-of-band discriminator. The 'r = 0.991' geo-vs-CGM correlation is also a dipole number (AACGM gives r = 0.999 over the eight European stations, which makes the overlap caveat even stronger). This comes from the ISS-2742 fix (closed 2026-06-16 via EXP-624), which introduced the dipole figures under a CGM label.
holes_found.recommendation: Find out which coordinate system Kim & Chang (2018) use for their 30-50° band (geomagnetic dipole or CGM/AACGM) and relabel to match. If they use dipole, change 'CGM' to 'geomagnetic (centered-dipole)' throughout and keep the numbers. If they use CGM, recompute band membership with AACGM and update the endpoint-station list, disclosing that the change is post-event. Either way, fix 'IAGA observatory registry' (the numbers weren't taken from a registry) and relabel the correlation coefficient.

holes_found.description: The dome prediction table our text cites was superseded by the dome before our pre-registration, and our own surfaces cite different dome values. detail_verdict_text says 'The dome publishes specific per-station delta_Z predictions for the 2026-08-12 European eclipse (EBR −10.7, SPT −9.8, ESK −10.3, LER −9.5, HAD −12.8, NGK −6.7, SNK −5.0, CLF −10.1, COI −10.1 nT)'. These come from the 2026-03-12 raw-text snapshot (raw-text/03-predictions.txt lines 21-31). The dome's live model page instructs 'Multiply all BOU-baseline predictions (E001–E009 BOU column) by 1.67' (monitor/baseline/05-model.txt line 475), and live predictions.html gives 'Magnitude: −17 to −21 nT at stations with >80% coverage (×1.672 correction applied 2026-03-28)', a 6-station Tier 1 priority list without LER, COI or the Canary station, and an audit table marking COI 'NO DATA' and LER '2023 data only'. Our KS-005 cites a different set again (−28.9 killshot, −17 to −21 homepage, −29.1 monitor.py; data/kill-shots.json KS-005 dome_prediction). The reconciliation is in monitor.py: −17.8 = −10.66 × 1.672 (corrected table), and −28.9 = −18.22 × 0.95 × 1.672, where −18.22 = −10.9 × 1.672, so the correction is applied twice and FSF is dropped. Two of our four named discriminating endpoints (LER, and SNK/Canary) aren't in the dome's live Tier 1 list, and the dome flags COI and LER data availability. The Canary station code 'SNK' is also not an INTERMAGNET IAGA code as far as we can find; the Canary observatory is GUI (Güímar), and our frozen file already writes 'SNK/GUI'.
holes_found.recommendation: Replace the present-tense 'publishes' with a dated list of every EBR value the dome has published (−10.7 BOU and −21.7 W004 from the 2026-03-12 table; −17.8 after the 2026-03-28 ×1.672 correction; −17 to −21 homepage range; −28.9 monitor.py, explained by the double-applied 1.672) and state which set the evaluation scores. Five prediction sets for one station strengthens the 'pick after the fact' argument already in the text. Align KS-005 and WIN-010 so both show the same reconciliation. Replace SNK with 'Canary Islands (dome label SNK; INTERMAGNET GUI)'. Note the dome's own station-availability flags for COI and LER.

holes_found.recommendation: Either (a) retitle to track the live claim (claim: '2016-03-09 quiet-day eclipse signal (formerly BOU 2017 −10.9 nT)') and add one TLDR clause each ('The dome has since swapped this WIN to a 2016 eclipse; the same Sq mechanism explains it'), or (b) keep the 2017 title but add to tldr_verdict: 'the dome has since withdrawn the 2017 event as storm-contaminated yet still scales its 2026 predictions from it'. Option (b) carries the stronger argument and costs about 20 words. Change tldr_verdict 'both confirmed WIN and 2026 baseline' to 'both a confirmed WIN (now WIN-012's coupling constant) and the 2026 baseline'.

holes_found.description: The text both grants the FSF as a genuine derivation and says it is trivial. detail_verdict_text para 2: 'Credit where it is due ... the field-strength factor genuinely does equal H(r)/r ... The dome is telling the truth about its geometric derivation — that piece of the argument should be granted.' Para 3: 'The scaling shape is not just non-unique — it is provably H(r)-independent ... not evidence of a fitted exponential height function'. detail_evidence: 'reproducible by a high schooler with a calculator'. Para 7 describes FSF as 'a function of geographic latitude through dome disc radius', which is stale because FSF is tan(geographic latitude) directly. The TLDR and finding keep only the 'genuinely derive' framing. A critic can quote these side by side. Cross-WIN, WIN-044 (verdict Self-Contradicted) treats the dome's FSF 'independently derived' claim as a fit, and ISS-2947 flagged the same grant-vs-inert tension in WIN-025.
holes_found.recommendation: State the reconciliation explicitly, once: 'The genuine dome content in FSF is V12 itself, the flat-geometry Polaris triangulation r·tan(θ) = H(r), which makes FSF = tan(lat)/tan(lat_BOU). The exponential H(r) and its 8537/8619 km constants are inert. So we grant that FSF is dome geometry, and note that the part the dome presents as its derivation (H(r)) contributes nothing.' Change para 7 to 'FSF = tan(lat)/tan(lat_BOU) profile'. Update finding and tldr_verdict to 'the station-to-station scaling (FSF) follows from the dome's flat Polaris-triangulation equation (it equals the ratio of tan(latitude)); its exponential height function plays no role'.

stronger_arguments.description: Dome self-contradiction: the dome scales every published 2026 prediction (the 2026-03-12 BOU column, the ×1.672-corrected −17 to −21 nT range, and monitor.py's −28.9 nT) from the 2017 BOU −10.9 nT value, which its own PROS-003 audit (2026-03-15) calls storm contamination with Z minima 'uncorrelated with eclipse geometry' and 'zero tracking stations'. The dome withdrew the event as evidence but kept it as the calibration for its only prospective eclipse prediction. This is a clean internal-consistency argument and doesn't depend on any of our physics.

The dome concedes the standard mechanism on its own predictions page: Tier 1 is headed 'Magnetic Signal (Globe-Compatible)' and lists as the globe prediction '0.0 nT systematic (or ionospheric Sq disruption — competing mechanism exists, see WIN-068 honest caveat)'. The live WIN-010 page says 'Globe has no mechanism predicting eclipse-correlated magnetic anomalies.' These two dome pages contradict each other, and the predictions page concedes our Std Model Explains verdict.

The dome's monitor.py can never record a result: the eclipse domain hardcodes observed='PENDING' and pass=None and has no INTERMAGNET fetch. Its falsification criterion is 'Fails if measured anomaly within ±3 nT of 0', so any |ΔB| > 3 nT counts as success, and the Sq mechanism guarantees that at 85-100% obscuration whenever the ionosphere is sunlit. This turns the poller's 'silent-ignore' observation into a code-level fact.

stronger_arguments.description: The dome's Kp rule has a gap that 2026 fell into. It says 'IF Kp < 2 ... will show', 'IF Kp ≥ 3 ... not a falsification', and nothing about 2 ≤ Kp < 3. GFZ eclipse-slot Kp on 2026-08-12 was 2.333. For WIN-011..014 cross-reference: the κ-protocol's C4 contact-phase prediction was untestable at EBR, SPT, CLF and NGK, where the sun was below the horizon at last contact (altitude at C4 −4.4°, −2.4°, −1.0°, −3.6°; Skyfield/DE421).

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome correctly identifies that eclipses produce measurable ground magnetic perturbations and that geomagnetic quietness matters for detecting them. Its live WIN-010 page contrasts the quiet 2016 event (BOU std 2.23 nT) with the noisier 2017 day (8.05 nT) (monitor/baseline/02-wins.txt lines 206, 222), and local variance is a reasonable detectability metric. Its FSF table really does follow from its V12 flat-triangulation equation (FSF = tan(lat)/tan(lat_BOU), r = 0.99991 recomputed this run against raw-text/03-predictions.txt lines 23-31), so the station scaling is internally consistent dome geometry. Pre-committing station-level numbers before 2026-08-12 was the right methodological move (raw-text/03-predictions.txt line 18, 'Registered 2026-03-12').
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The magnitude is imported, not derived: −10.9 nT from BOU 2017, then ×1.672 (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt 'Magnitude ... ×1.672 correction'). That anchor has been disowned by the dome's own audit (monitor/baseline/02-wins.txt line 73), the dome's coverage inputs are wrong by up to ×2.1 at NGK and LER against ephemeris obscuration, and its own Kp precondition failed on the event (GFZ 2026-08-12 eclipse slot Kp 2.333). The dome's predictions page also concedes that Sq disruption is a 'competing mechanism' for the Tier 1 signal (monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt, TIER 1 block). A correct detectability heuristic plus self-consistent scaling of a borrowed number doesn't make the observed signal a dome prediction.

advocate_mode.best_defense: 'Your review lectures us about Kp, but GFZ shows our 2017 anchor was at Kp 1+ during the eclipse (you said Kp ≈ 3) and our 2016 re-anchor was at Kp 2 (you called it genuinely Kp<2). You got both backwards and blasted us for the same kind of Kp error in WIN-025. On 2026: we pre-stated that Kp ≥ 2 conditions void the test, the window hit Kp 3.0 and the eclipse slot 2.33, so by our pre-registered rule it is not a falsification. Your own frozen file says the same thing (B1-M-001: Kp ≥ 2 is not a falsification of either model). And where is YOUR nine-station test? You promised to update when data arrived, INTERMAGNET data has been public since mid-August, and your own page set 11 September as the evaluation date. You call our silence tacit withdrawal while doing the same thing. Your frozen Hartland obscuration looks wrong by ~6 points, and your 'CGM' latitudes aren't CGM.'
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Most of this defense is valid, and the fix is to concede and correct quickly rather than argue: (1) correct both Kp statements from GFZ (hole 0); (2) publish a dated post-event status now, even if the analysis is 'overdue, in progress', so our silence isn't comparable to the dome's (hole 1); (3) apply the Kp caveat symmetrically, since we pre-registered the same non-falsification rule; (4) if confirmed, disclose the Hartland B1-G-005 miss ourselves before a defender finds it (hole 4); (5) fix the CGM label (hole 5). Once those are done, the defense reduces to 'the test was voided by conditions', and the self-contradiction (stronger_arguments[0]), the double-applied 1.672 and the coverage-input errors still stand. The Std Model Explains verdict doesn't depend on any of the points the defender scores.

cross_win_consistency.inconsistencies_found: (1) WIN-025 audits the dome's Kp claim against GFZ and finds it factually wrong. WIN-010 states Kp values for 2017 and 2016 without that audit, and GFZ contradicts both, so the method isn't applied uniformly (hole 0). (2) KS-005 and WIN-010 cite different dome prediction values for EBR (−28.9/−17 to −21/−29.1 vs −10.7/−21.7), with no reconciliation on either surface (hole 6). (3) WIN-044 (Self-Contradicted) treats the dome's FSF as a fit, while WIN-010's TLDR and finding grant it as a genuine derivation. That's compatible once V12 vs H(r) is spelled out, but the text doesn't do it (hole 8; same class as ISS-2947 on WIN-025). (4) WIN-012 carries the −10.9 κ numerator 'unchanged'. The dome's PROS-003 disowning of 2017 as storm contamination bears on WIN-012's evidence base too, and a cross-reference should be added there. (5) WIN-010, WIN-025 and WIN-068 share the Sq mechanism (existing detail_group note), which is consistent.

deeper_analysis: Why this is a major_rewrite and not a verdict change: every hole concerns the 2017/2016 evidentiary framing, the 2026 pre-registration mechanics, or cross-surface consistency. None touches the core claim that Chapman Sq explains eclipse magnetic dips without dome geometry, and the stronger_arguments strengthen that claim (the dome's own 'Globe-Compatible' concession, and the self-contradicting calibration). Std Model Explains holds. Priority order for the decider: hole 0 (Kp facts; a defender can check it in 30 seconds) > hole 1 (post-event status; every day of silence weakens the tacit-withdrawal argument against the dome) > hole 4 (possible frozen-claim miss; must be disclosed by us, not found by them) > holes 2, 3 > 5-9. The pipeline-health context matters: poller reports most dome agents disabled since around 2026-08-17/18, which probably explains why the post-eclipse evaluation stalled. That's an operational cause, not an excuse the public page can offer. Other side of the argument: the Skyfield obscuration and AACGM numbers are my computations and should be independently confirmed before anyone asserts them in prose. The GFZ Kp values are definitive-status ('def') and are the most solid findings here. On hole 1, it's defensible that our frozen B1-M-001 amplitude window (−25 to −5 nT) is a real standard-physics prediction that could still be scored cleanly regardless of Kp, so we aren't in the same position as the dome, provided we actually score it.
